title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates 38th Pune Festival
subtitle:
“Nation Must Never Forget Its History and Sacrifices of Its Heroes”: Vice-President

Vice-President Recalls Legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Lokmanya Tilak, Mahatma Phule, Savitribai Phule and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

“Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s Contribution to Preserving Hindu Dharma and Civilisational Heritage Must Be Remembered”: Vice-President

Vice-President Presents Founder Suresh Kalmadi Pune Festival Lifetime Achievement Award to Shri Mohan Joshi

“Development Must Go Hand in Hand with Preservation of Heritage”: Vice-President Reaffirms PM’s “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi” Vision
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 38th Pune Festival at Shri Ganesh Kala Krida Rangmanch, Pune.
Maharashtra Governor Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Deputy Chief Minister Smt. Sunetra Pawar, Minister for Higher & Technical Education Shri Chandrakant Patil, Minister for Cultural Affairs Shri Ashish Shelar, MP Smt. Hema Malini, MP Dr. Medha Kulkarni and former Union Home Minister Shri Sushil kumar Shinde were among those present.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 38th Pune Festival in Pune today.
The Vice President said that Pune has emerged as a major centre of education, industry, sports, information technology, automobile manufacturing, tourism and horticulture, while retaining…

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)

The Vice-President said that the nation must never forget its history and the great sacrifices made by its heroes. Recalling the enduring legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, he said that his contribution to the preservation of Hindu Dharma and India’s civilisational heritage must always be remembered. He also highlighted the deep historical and cultural bonds between Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, noting that Tamil literary works have been preserved at the Saraswathi Mahal Library in Thanjavur because of Maratha leaders .
He also paid tribute to Lokmanya Tilak, Mahatma Jyotiba Phule, Krantijyoti Savitribai Phule and Babasaheb B. R. Ambedkar.
Appreciating Pune’s growing global character, the Vice-President particularly lauded the performance of international students at the inauguration session. He noted that students from around 20 countries participated in Traditional Ganesh Worship programme , describing it as a beautiful manifestation of the spirit of “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.”
The Vice-President said Pune has emerged as a major centre of education, industry, sports, information technology, automobile manufacturing, tourism and horticulture, while retaining its cultural identity. He credited the Pune Festival with contributing significantly to Pune’s emergence as a “City of Festivals” and appreciated the vision of its founder, late Shri Suresh Kalmadi.
Appreciating the festival’s focus on young and emerging artists, the Vice-President highlighted programmes such as Ugavate Tare and Indradhanu. He also commended the Mahila Mahotsav for providing women artists a platform to showcase their talent and creativity.
Emphasising the need to remain rooted in India’s civilisational heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that development must go hand in hand with preservation of heritage. Referring to the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi,” he said modernity and technological advancement need not come at the cost of traditions and cultural values.
The Vice-President said the vision of Viksit Bharat encompasses not only economic growth and infrastructure but also an inclusive and equitable society rooted in its civilisational heritage. He noted that festivals such as the Pune Festival can promote cultural exchange, tourism, local talent and national integration.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan prayed to Lord Ganesha for continued unity, harmony and service, and expressed the hope that the Pune Festival would continue to celebrate India’s composite culture, inspire young talent, empower women, promote tourism and strengthen national integration.
The Vice-President also presented the Founder Suresh Kalmadi Pune Festival Lifetime Achievement Award to veteran actor Shri Mohan Joshi, recognising his distinguished contribution to Indian cinema and the performing arts.

content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis at Kaivalyadhama, Lonavala, Maharashtra.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of Gordhandas Seksaria College of Yoga and Cultural Synthesis at Kaivalyadhama, Lonavala.
Congratulating the College on completing 75 years of dedicated service to Yoga education, research and…

He congratulated the College on completing 75 years of dedicated service to Yoga education, research and cultural synthesis. He noted that the occasion was especially significant as Kaivalyadhama itself has completed a century of dedicated service to Yoga.
Recalling the contribution of Swami Kuvalayananda, who founded Kaivalyadhama in 1924, the Vice-President said that he pioneered the scientific study of Yoga at a time when it was largely viewed as a mystical practice. He emphasised that the legacies of the past must be preserved and carried forward for future generations. “Yoga is not for one generation; it is for every generation to come,” he said.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the growing global acceptance of Yoga and recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s sustained efforts in taking its message to the international stage. He noted that Yoga is today practised across nations, cultures and communities.
Observing that technological progress and digital connectivity have made life increasingly fast-paced, the Vice-President said Yoga provides an opportunity to pause, concentrate, reflect and reconnect with oneself. He said Yoga helps bridge the gap between mind and body and promotes physical and mental well-being.
Addressing the young students, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said India’s youth possess immense energy, talent and ambition, which achieve their fullest potential when combined with discipline and awareness. Referring to Patanjali’s concept of chitta vritti nirodhah, he said the ability to calm and focus the mind is particularly relevant in an age of constant notifications and information overload.
The Vice-President said that any endeavour undertaken with good intention and with a sincere commitment to the well-being of society can leave a lasting legacy. Good legacies never die; they continue to inspire and benefit generations to come. The century-long journey of Kaivalyadhama is a living testament to this enduring truth.
The Vice-President congratulated the Trustees, Principal, faculty, students and alumni of the College and paid tribute to the vision of Swami Kuvalayananda and the contribution of Seth Makhanlal Seksaria.
On the occasion, the Vice-President also launched “Yoga Explained – Learn From the Master” by Shri O. P. Tiwari. He visited the campus and interacted with the students, encouraging them to cultivate the values of discipline, concentration and self-awareness through the practice of Yoga.
Governor of Maharashtra Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, former Union Minister and Chairman of Kaivalyadhama Global Shri Suresh Prabhu, CEO of Kaivalyadhama Global Shri Subodh Tiwari, Chief Patron Shri Rakesh Seksaria, faculty members, students, alumni and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: PM to inaugurate International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September
subtitle:
Conference to facilitate dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance

Conference to witness participation of eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries and distinguished participants from India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” on 19 September 2026 at around 10 AM at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi.
The two-day Conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal on 19 and 20 September 2026. It will witness the participation of environmental experts, Judges of the Supreme Court of India and High Courts, District Court Judges, Secretaries of various Ministries, senior government officials, representatives of State Judicial Academies, State Legal Services Authorities, State Expert Appraisal Committees (SEACs), State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAAs), State Wetland Authorities and other stakeholders. It will also bring together eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries.
The Conference will provide a platform for the exchange of judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences across jurisdictions. It will facilitate dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement, and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for Time-Bound Action on State Commitments at Southern Regional Agriculture Conference
subtitle:
No Eating, Meeting and Sitting; We Must Deliver Results. Otherwise, It Would Amount to Cheating the People: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Centre, States, Scientists and Farmers Are One Agriculture Team; We Must Work Together to Transform Farming: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Farmer ID and AgriStack Work Must Be Completed Within Deadlines; No State Should Be Left Behind: Union Agriculture Minister

Research Must Reach Farmers, From Lab to Land; India Must Become the World’s Food Basket: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Bharat Vistar to Reach Farmers in 13 Regional Languages; Rabi Conference in Delhi on September 28–29: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, while addressing the concluding session of the Regional Agriculture Conference for Southern States in Hyderabad, directed states to complete their agricultural targets and commitments within the stipulated timelines. He said states must act seriously on the actionable points identified during the day-long deliberations. The conference, he emphasised, must translate into concrete action and measurable outcomes. “The Centre and the states are one agriculture team. Our scientists, our farmers, officers of the Central and state governments, all together form one agriculture team. We must work together,” Shri Chouhan said. He stressed that commitments made by states at the conference must be fulfilled. Otherwise, the entire exercise would lose its purpose. If a state has committed to completing Farmer ID generation by December, it must meet that deadline, he said. There is no need to repeat discussions on every issue, but action on the decisions taken is essential.
The objective is results, not just meetings
Shri Chouhan said the conference would serve no purpose if the decisions taken were not implemented. “If we come for a day, eat, meet and sit, and do nothing beyond that, it would amount to cheating the people. That is not what we want. We have to deliver results,” he said. Expressing confidence in the agriculture teams working at the Centre and in the states, he said all levels must work together to bring about meaningful change in the sector. “Creating a commotion is not my objective. My desire is to change the situation. We will change the face of agriculture,” Shri Chouhan said. He also recalled the commitment made during the Viksit Krishi Sankalp Abhiyan that whenever states finalise dates for their agricultural outreach programmes, scientists from the Government of India and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) would accompany them. Scientists will visit villages and fields, sit with farmers and hold discussions involving farmers, scientists and agriculture department officials. The objective is to strengthen direct engagement between agricultural research and farming communities.
States asked to accelerate work on Farmer ID and AgriStack
Shri Chouhan said states would have understood the importance of AgriStack and noted the progress made in generating Farmer IDs. Telangana and Karnataka have crossed 75% completion in Farmer ID generation, he said. Good progress has also been made in georeferencing in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana. He said Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have achieved completion in the Digital Crop Survey. However, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands still need to accelerate work on Farmer ID generation, he said. Shri Chouhan stressed that Farmer ID work must be completed within the stipulated deadlines, as several agricultural systems in the coming years will depend on it. “I expect that no state should be left behind,” he said.
Land records and Farmer Registry must be integrated
The Union Agriculture Minister said states where land parcels have not yet been linked must expedite the process, particularly Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Kerala also needs to ensure coordination between land record data and the Farmer Registry, he said. He called for the preparation and notification of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for tenant farmers, including sharecroppers and agricultural tenants, in southern states. Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands need to take up work in this area, he said. He also directed Puducherry and Lakshadweep to undertake georeferencing of village maps.
Bharat Vistar to reach farmers in 13 regional languages
Shri Chouhan said farmers face several challenges every day and cannot be expected to travel to different offices for advice on every issue. To address this, Bharat Vistar has been developed to provide farmers with access to appropriate advice through a mobile phone. The system is currently available in Hindi and English and will be expanded to 13 regional languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. Farmers will be able to ask questions in their own language and receive answers in the same language. Referring to the participation of the Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister, who spoke in Telugu, Shri Chouhan said expressing ideas in one’s own language makes communication more precise and effective. “Farmers understand their own language. Therefore, we must work with the states to complete this system at the earliest,” he said. He also directed that state government schemes be integrated with Bharat Vistar as quickly as possible.
Research must reach farmers from lab to land
Shri Chouhan said states could schedule 15-day or 20-day agricultural campaigns according to their convenience, and scientists from the Government of India would visit the states during these campaigns. “We have 16,000 scientists,” he said, highlighting the role of ICAR institutions, KVKs and agricultural universities. These institutions are not only meant to conduct research but also to ensure that research reaches farmers, he said. “Unless farmers and scientists sit together, and unless research reaches the farmer, it will not be enough. Research must move from lab to land,” Shri Chouhan said.
India must become the world’s leading agricultural nation
Shri Chouhan said he wanted to work with complete dedication and honesty to make India a global leader in agriculture. “We have to make India the world’s food basket. It can be done. It is not impossible. It will happen, but all of us have to work for it,” he said. He noted that Indian agriculture has undergone significant transformation and said further changes would be pursued to establish India as a global leader in the sector.
Rabi Conference to be held in Delhi on September 28–29
Shri Chouhan announced that the Rabi Conference would be held at the Pusa Institute in Delhi on September 28 and 29. Agriculture Ministers and officials from all states will attend the conference with their respective teams and bring detailed plans for the Rabi season. The conference will finalise decisions on the crops to be sown during Rabi and the area to be brought under each crop. Based on these plans, the availability of seeds, fertiliser requirements and other essential resources will be assessed, and further preparations will be undertaken.
The conference was also attended by Ministers of State for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary along with Ministers of Agriculture from states of Telangana, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Puducherry.
Senior officers from the Ministry, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Atish Chandra, and Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR Dr. M. L. Jat also  participated in the conference.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Addresses Southern States Regional Agriculture Conference in Hyderabad, Focuses on Farmers’ Incomes and Agricultural Growth
subtitle:
Nation First, It Does Not Matter Which Government Is in Power in a State: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

If Old Acts and Procedures Need Change, States Should Come Forward with Suggestions: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Prime Minister Modi Has Said: Government Must Be Visible in People’s Lives, Not Just in Files: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Machines Can Make Bread, But They Cannot Grow Wheat; The World Cannot Run Without Agriculture: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Every State Has Different Conditions, Making Regional Agriculture Conferences Essential: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Food Security, Farmers’ Livelihoods and Nutrition Security Are the Three Key Goals of Agriculture: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Southern India Has Huge Horticulture Potential; Focus on Maximising Benefits for Coconut and Cashew Farmers: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today addressed the Regional Agriculture Conference for the Southern States in Hyderabad, with discussions focusing on key challenges and opportunities facing agriculture in the region. The conference discussed the impact of El Niño, crop diversification and the measures required for the upcoming Rabi season. Shri Chouhan said the deliberations were not an exercise in discussion alone, but were aimed at bringing tangible improvements in farmers’ lives, strengthening India’s food security, expanding employment opportunities through agriculture and giving fresh momentum to the economy through the farm sector. 'Nation First' is the guiding principle of the government, Shri Chouhan said, adding that the Centre does not approach agricultural issues on the basis of which political party is in power in a state. The focus, he said, is on finding solutions that can improve the lives of farmers under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.
Machines can make bread, but they cannot grow wheat
Shri Chouhan said technological progress, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics and other modern technologies, would continue to transform the world, but agriculture would remain indispensable. “Fruits, vegetables and grains can only come from the farm, and farmers are the ones who produce them. The world cannot function without agriculture,” he said. A machine may be able to make bread, he said, but it cannot produce wheat. “Grain will always have to be grown in the field. That is why a farmer is not only an ‘Annadata’ but also a ‘Jeevandata’,” he said. Shri Chouhan said serving farmers was, for him, akin to serving God because agriculture is fundamental to human life. He outlined three key objectives for Indian agriculture. The first is to ensure food security for a population of more than 140 crore. He said this has become even more important in the present circumstances and India cannot afford to depend on the world for its food requirements. The second objective is to secure farmers’ livelihoods. The farmer who feeds the nation must also live a secure and prosperous life, and increasing farmers’ incomes must remain a key priority. The third objective is nutritional security. Ensuring that people have access not just to food, but to nutritious food, must also remain central to agricultural policy. Shri Chouhan highlighted the immense potential for horticulture in southern India, particularly in spices, coffee, cashew, cocoa, sandalwood and other crops. These sectors, he said, also have an important role to play in strengthening nutritional security.
Regional agriculture conferences essential for region-specific planning
Shri Chouhan said India’s agricultural landscape is marked by significant diversity. While the country earlier held a single Rabi conference, states have different agro-climatic zones, resources, water availability and soil conditions. “It is not possible to sit at one place for a day and prepare a common Rabi or Kharif plan for the entire country,” he said. The Rabi conference was therefore expanded from one day to two days, allowing each state greater opportunity to present its concerns, challenges and suggestions. The Centre can also place its expectations before the states and jointly work towards an agricultural roadmap. Shri Chouhan said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also emphasised the importance of regional conferences. The challenges faced by Jammu and Kashmir, Gujarat or the Northeast, he said, cannot necessarily be the same as those faced by Andhra Pradesh or Telangana. Different geographical and climatic conditions require different approaches to farming. The Southern Regional Agriculture Conference has been organised with this understanding and to develop solutions suited to the specific needs of the region.
Rules should serve people, not become a burden on them
Shri Chouhan said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has placed strong emphasis on reforms and called for a review of rules, laws and procedures that may need to be changed. “Rules are meant for people; people are not meant for rules,” he said. He urged state governments to review outdated Acts and procedures and make changes wherever necessary. If any issue requires intervention at the level of the Government of India, states should communicate it openly, he said. The Prime Minister has repeatedly emphasised that government should be visible in people’s lives and not confined to files, Shri Chouhan said. Wherever changes in rules are required, states should put forward their suggestions. The Centre will undertake necessary reforms at its level, while states should make changes within their jurisdiction to provide greater relief to citizens.
States should learn from best practices and jointly build an agricultural roadmap
Shri Chouhan said the conference would include presentations and discussions on various agricultural issues, followed by interaction with farmers and other stakeholders to seek their suggestions. Best practices from different states would also be presented so that successful initiatives in one state could be adapted by others. He noted that southern states have undertaken significant work in agriculture and horticulture and congratulated them for their achievements, while emphasising that there remains scope for further improvement. “The Government of India will support the states with full strength. Land is with the states, farmers are in the states, and the Centre will provide all possible support. Both must work together,” he said. Reiterating the principle of 'Nation First', Shri Chouhan said Centre-State cooperation is essential for taking agriculture forward and is one of the key reasons why regional conferences are important.
Coconut exports grow 62% in one year
Highlighting the potential of the coconut sector, Shri Chouhan said India’s coconut exports increased from ₹4,349 crore to ₹7,038 crore in one year, registering a growth of 62%. He said a new scheme for promotion of coconut has been announced in the Budget and is now set to become operational. Since southern states are the country’s leaders in coconut production, they should begin preparations to take full advantage of the new initiative. He also called for a strategy to rejuvenate old coconut plantations. Coconut trees that are 60–70 years old often produce fewer coconuts and may not provide the desired quality, he said. States should therefore consider gradually replacing old trees with new plantations in phases. Shri Chouhan also urged states to prepare in advance for the promotion schemes for cashew and cocoa so that farmers in these sectors can derive maximum benefit.
FTAs opening new opportunities for Indian farmers in global markets
Shri Chouhan said India has entered into several Free Trade Agreements with countries around the world under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. These agreements have facilitated market access for a range of agricultural products, including fruits, vegetables and grains. He called for a detailed study of these agreements to identify products in demand in international markets and to align domestic production accordingly. Farmers should be encouraged to produce fruits, vegetables and grains that meet international quality requirements, he said. International standards should be adopted across the agricultural value chain so that Indian farmers can benefit from expanding global markets. “The markets of the world are opening up for India, and this is an opportunity for farmers,” Shri Chouhan said, urging all stakeholders to deliberate seriously on the Rabi season and other issues related to agriculture.
Telangana to get 2 lakh houses under PMAY-G
Shri Chouhan said the present state government has taken the initiative and the first instalment from the Government of India for construction of 2 lakh houses has been handed over to the Chief Minister of Telangana. Construction of these 2 lakh houses will now begin, he said. Shri Chouhan added that beneficiaries whose houses are still kutcha and who have been identified through the survey would also be covered in subsequent phases. The Centre will continue to extend full support to Telangana across sectors, he said. The Southern Regional Agriculture Conference brings together the Centre, southern states and Union Territories, agricultural experts, ICAR institutions, progressive farmers and other stakeholders to deliberate on region-specific agricultural priorities and strengthen coordination for sustainable and resilient agriculture.

title: 25th Meeting of SCO Ministers Responsible for Economic and Foreign Trade Activities Held in Tajikistan

date:

                18 SEP 2026 12:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 25th Meeting of Ministers of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States Responsible for Foreign Economic and Trade Activities was held in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on 17 September 2026.
The Meeting reviewed ongoing cooperation among SCO Member States in the areas of economic and trade activities and exchanged views on measures to further deepen trade and economic cooperation within the SCO framework.
In his intervention on behalf of India, Shri Yashvir Singh, highlighted the significant economic potential of the SCO and the importance of translating this potential into tangible outcomes through increased intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, resilient supply chains and enhanced connectivity.
Referring to the vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit in Bishkek, India highlighted the three pillars of Security, Connectivity and Opportunity. India underscored their economic significance, particularly in strengthening supply-chain resilience, developing efficient and trusted connectivity, and expanding opportunities for businesses through greater market access.
India emphasised the important role of trade facilitation and digitalisation in reducing the cost and time associated with trade. In this context, India highlighted the need for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade and electronic exchange of documents, alongside stronger multimodal connectivity and reduced transit times.
India also called for greater cooperation among SCO Member States to diversify and strengthen supply chains in strategic and emerging sectors, including agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing and electronics. The potential for enhanced cooperation in energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen was also highlighted.
Recognising the importance of enabling smaller businesses to participate more effectively in regional and global trade, India underscored the role of digital payments, cross-border payments and accessible trade finance, particularly for MSMEs and start-ups. India further called for greater participation of SCO economies in global value chains and reiterated its commitment to an open, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.
The Ministers adopted the ‘Statement of the Ministers of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States Responsible for Foreign Economic and Foreign Trade Activity’.
The Ministers agreed on the ‘Action Plan for 2026–2030 for the Implementation of the Programme of Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States’ for its further approval by the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the SCO Member States.
The Ministers also approved the ‘Regulations on the Special Working Group of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States on the Development of the Creative Economy’.
The Ministers took note of the information provided by the representative of the SCO Business Council regarding the activities of the Council. They also took note of the information provided by the Tajik side on the work of the SCO Consortium of Economic Analytical Centres.
The Ministers noted that the next Ministerial Meeting will be held in 2027 in the Republic of Uzbekistan.

The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Government of India, Shri Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary, Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Government of Nepal, Shri Buddha Bahadur Gurung. Senior officials from the concerned Ministries and Departments of both countries participated in the meeting.
The IGSC is an important bilateral institutional mechanism for detailed examination of trade and trade-related issues and for facilitating bilateral trade and transit.
During the meeting, both sides reviewed a wide range of issues relating to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, phytosanitary measures, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, AYUSH products, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters.
Both sides discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of India and Nepal. Issues relating to agricultural products, dairy, food products, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and AYUSH products, along with standards and phytosanitary requirements, were considered.
The two sides also discussed strengthening Customs cooperation and trade facilitation, including pre-arrival exchange of information, electronic verification of Certificates of Origin, Customs automation and digitalisation. The discussions focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements.
Transit and connectivity constituted an important part of the discussions. Both sides reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure. The discussions also focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade.
The two sides welcomed continued cooperation in standards, food safety, plant quarantine and conformity assessment, including institutional cooperation and capacity-building initiatives.
Both sides emphasised the importance of continued cooperation between the relevant agencies to facilitate legitimate cross-border trade and address issues relating to unauthorised trade and commercial fraud.
The meeting was held in a cordial and constructive atmosphere. Both sides agreed to maintain close engagement through established institutional mechanisms and pursue time-bound follow-up on issues requiring further technical examination.

The discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

title: TRAI Strengthens Framework for Curbing Unsolicited Commercial Communications through Technology-Driven Enforcement and Enhanced Consumer Protection
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has amended the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR, 2018) to further strengthen the regulatory framework for curbing Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC), protect consumers from spam and prevent misuse of telecom resources for sending UCC.
TRAI issued “Draft Telecom Commercial Communication Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026” for Consultation on 13th March 2026 to seek stakeholders' views on key regulatory amendments needed to strengthen the existing regulatory framework, enhance enforcement mechanisms and address emerging challenges in the prevention and regulation of UCC. The consultation focused on several vital issues, including leveraging AI/ML-based suspected UCC detection to aid in regulatory enforcement, strengthening mechanism for complaint-based action, expanding scope of explicit consent to accommodate legacy consents available with the entities, providing for appeal mechanism, strengthening the accountability of Senders and Telemarketers, regulating Application-to-Person (A2P) calls, strengthening safeguards against the misuse of Headers and Content Templates etc.
The comments and counter-comments on the draft regulations were received till 19th April, 2026, and 04th May, 2026, respectively. The Open House Discussion (OHD) with the stakeholders was held on 3rd June, 2026. After considering stakeholders’ feedback and carrying out detailed analysis, the Authority has introduced the Telecom Commercial Communication Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026 today.
SALIENT FEATURES OF THE AMENDMENTS
(i) Leveraging AI/ML-based suspected UCC detection to aid in regulatory enforcement
(a) Major Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have already deployed AI/ML-based systems to detect suspected spam communications and alert the customers. The Authority also issued a Direction on 27th February, 2026 to the TSPs for using AI/ML-based intelligence on suspected UCC for inter-operator sharing and to carry out further investigation of suspected UCC senders.
(b) The provisions of the said Direction have been suitably incorporated into the TCCCPR, 2018 through the introduction of Regulation 21A which mandates the TSPs to identify the sender’s CLIs having a high probability of being used for sending UCC and share the information among the TSPs.
(c) Where five or more CLIs (Calling Line Identification) associated with a Sender are flagged within a period of ten days, further investigation and graded action will be initiated by the Access Providers, including KYC re-verification, physical verification, barring of outgoing services, and disconnection of telecom resource in cases of repeated violations and misuse of telecom resources.
(d) Special numbering series designated for commercial communications, including the 140xx, 1600xx and 1601xx series, shall not be flagged as suspected spam for recipients, thereby ensuring that legitimate commercial communications and government communications from the regulated series are not inadvertently missed.
(ii) Regulation of Application-to-Person (A2P) calls
(a) Application-to-Person (A2P) calling is being used for bulk commercial communications due to its ability to automate and scale large volumes of calls, and therefore, there exists a potential for their misuse for making spam calls.
(b) Accordingly, to regulate such calling, the amendments have defined A2P calls as voice calls initiated by an application, software system or automated platform without direct human dialing, including using autodialing, robo-calls and pre-recorded/artificial voice technologies. It has been mandated that every entity using A2P calls must pre-declare such use to its TSP along with the details of CLIs to be used for making such calls.
A2P calls made without the required prior declaration will be treated as UCC.
(c) To act as a deterrent, a termination charge of up to ₹0.05 per minute has been introduced to be levied by the Terminating Access Provider on the Originating Access Provider for A2P calls.
(d)
A2P calls made through any numbering series designated by the Authority for regulated commercial calls, and Authority-authorized calls are exempted from termination charges
.
(iii) Commercial Communications based on inquiry:
(a) Commercial communications may be sent to a customer on the basis of an inquiry made by the customer to the sender for goods or products or services, only for a period of seven days from the date of such inquiry.
(b) However, to prevent the misuse of such provision for sending spam, it has been mandated that such an inquiry shall be made in writing or through digital means, and shall be maintained in a verifiable form by the Sender.
(c)
The amendment is intended primarily to facilitate e-Commerce and e-Service Platforms.
(iv) Introduction of Consumer Appeal Mechanism
(a) Consumers will now be able to prefer an appeal against the resolution of UCC complaints. The appeal may be preferred within 15 days before the Appellate Authority.
(b) Appeals will be resolved by the Appellate Authority as per the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (TCCR) Regulations, 2012.
(c) The appeal may be preferred through any of the modes available for lodging UCC complaints i.e. through TRAI DND App, TSPs App/Portal, and call or SMS to 1909 besides the modes specified under TCCRR, 2012.
(v) Strengthening of Complaint-Based Action against UCC
(a) The existing regulations provide a complaint threshold of 5 or more unique complaints within a period of ten days to trigger action against the UCC Sender.
(b) To enable early identification of UCC senders and faster action against them, the amendments have mandated corroboration of the complaint data received from consumers with the data of Senders detected by service provider’s AI systems as suspected of sending UCC with high probability.
(c) Action will be triggered against the sender if there are 3 or more unique complaints within a period of ten days and the concerned Sender’s CLI is also flagged by the AI/ML-based system as suspected of sending UCC.
(d) Certain timelines prescribed under the complaint mechanism have been revised keeping in view the practical time required for implementation.
(vi) Expanded Scope of Explicit Consent
The definition of consent has been expanded to include legacy consents already available with the entities. The framework is being amended to enable the recognition and digitization of such legacy consents. However, the legacy consents shall be considered valid only where they have been obtained through verifiable means and are subsequently registered on the Digital Platform of the TSPs.
(vii) Strengthening Measures against Misuse of Headers and Content Templates
(a)  In cases involving misuse of Headers or Content Templates, the Originating Access Provider shall suspend the misused Headers or Content Templates, within six hours of becoming aware of such misuse, and issue a notice to the concerned Sender within the prescribed period.
(b) The concerned Sender shall be required to undertake specified remedial measures to prevent any further misuse, and file a complaint with the appropriate law enforcement agency. Where the misuse is attributed to a Telemarketer, all its telecom resources across the TSPs will be disconnected for a period of one year, along with blacklisting.
(viii) Essential conditions of Agreement between Access Providers and Senders/Telemarketers
(a) Under the regulatory framework, the TSPs have been obligated to ensure compliance of the regulatory provisions by the Senders and Telemarketer through contractual obligations between them.  However, it has been observed that TSPs many times do not put strict conditions in the agreements to ensure compliance by these entities, primarily due to competition issues.
(b) Accordingly, to have more effective action against the Senders and Telemarketers engaged in sending UCC, a new provision has been introduced whereby the Authority may prescribe the essential conditions that must mandatorily form part of these agreements between the Access Providers and the Senders/ Telemarketers.
(ix) Classification of Senders
There exists a variety of Senders based on considerations such as the criticality of the services and the sector to which a Sender belongs, the importance of the entity to the economy, scale of operations, extent of usage of telecom resources by the Sender, and the potential impact of suspending/ disconnecting telecom resources of the Sender on the consumers. A new regulation has been introduced whereby the Authority may classify the Senders into different categories and may specify differentiated sets of enforcement measures applicable to such categories of Senders for violations of the regulations.
(x) Prohibition on blanket blocking/tagging by Call Management Applications
(a) Call Management Applications (CMAs) are prohibited from blanket blocking, filtering, or spam tagging calls from number series designated by the Authority or the Central Government for commercial communication such as 1600xx/1601xx for service and transactional calls, and 140xx for
regulated
promotional calls, since such tagging, without the safeguards built into the regulatory mechanism, risks mislabeling genuine commercial communications and government communications as spam, which are otherwise important to customers. However, individual consumers retain full freedom to block, or filter calls on their own devices.
(b) To facilitate wider collation of data for action against spammers, it has also been mandated that no CMA shall offer the users to report any unsolicited commercial communication under any name such as spam, junk, etc. on its platform, unless the CMA sends such report to the DLT platform maintained by the Access Providers.
(xi) Digital Interface for VNOs with the DLT Platform
As Virtual Network Operators (VNOs) are also Access Provider under the regulatory framework, the Network Service Operator (NSO) will be required to provide the VNO a digital interface having real-time functionality with the DLT platform and other systems necessary for the VNO to discharge its obligations as an Access Provider under the Regulations. This will address the operational difficulty presently being faced by the VNOs with respect to the access to the DLT Platform.
The amendments are aimed at strengthening consumer confidence in the commercial communication ecosystem, ensuring greater accountability across stakeholders, and enabling more effective and timely action against misuse of telecom resources by the spammers.
For further information, Shri Deepak Sharma, Advisor (QoS-Il), TRAI, may be contacted at 011-20907760 or at email-id advqos@trai.gov.in

title: Government Relaxes Sugar Stockholding Limit for Bulk Consumers from 15 to 30 Days, Additional stock to be sourced exclusively from imported sugar under Advance Authorization Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ)
subtitle: Retail Sugar Prices Decline by Around 10%; Government Urges Traders, wholesalers & Retailers to Pass on Benefit of Lower Ex-Mill Prices to Consumers
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 2:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government has decided that the existing 15 days’ stockholding limit for bulk consumers is relaxed to 30 days, subject to the condition that the quantity of stock held beyond the existing 15 days’ limit, shall be sourced exclusively from sugar imported under Advance Authorisation Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ).
The stockholding limit for purchase from the open market shall remain unchanged and will be restricted to 15 days’ consumption only. The government has also put in place a mechanism for the declaration and
weekly disclosure of sugar stocks every Friday
by bulk consumers through the Department of Food and Public Distribution's online portal @
https://foodstock.dfpd.gov.in/
The Government has held detailed consultations with major bulk consumers of sugar and their suggestions have been duly considered with a view to maintaining a stable and orderly sugar market.
At present, bulk consumers using or consuming more than 10 MT of sugar per month as a raw material for production, consumption or use are permitted to hold sugar stock for a period not exceeding 15 days of their consumption.  Bulk consumers have represented that the existing limit may be enhanced, particularly in view of the upcoming festival season. They also suggested that they may be permitted to directly source sugar from importers holding sugar imported under Advance Authorisation Scheme and Tariff Rate Quota, so as to ensure uninterrupted availability of sugar for industrial consumption without adversely affecting domestic supplies.
The measure is intended to strike a balance between the interests of bulk consumers and the need to maintain stability in the domestic sugar market. It will provide greater operational flexibility to genuine industrial consumers during the upcoming festival season while ensuring that additional stocks are sourced from imported sugar rather than placing undue pressure on domestic stocks.
Retail sugar prices declined by 10%
Retail sugar prices have declined by around 10% from their peak
(Rs. 65 in August to Rs. 58.50)
. However, ex-mill prices have already declined by nearly 25%. The Government observed that the slower decline in retail prices indicates that the benefit of the reduction in ex-mill prices has not yet been fully transmitted through the supply chain to the consumer.
In a joint meeting held today with representatives of ISMA, the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories and sugar trade, Secretary, Department of Food and Public Distribution, underlined that the reduction in ex-mill prices has not yet been reflected fully in retail prices.
The Government today made a strong appeal to the sugar traders, wholesalers & retailers to immediately pass on the benefit of the significant reduction in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers, emphasising that the decline in retail prices must keep pace with the correction already achieved at the mill level. The Government called upon the entire sugar value chain to collectively ensure that sugar and sugar-based products remain affordable and within the reach of consumers during the forthcoming festivals.
The Secretary emphasised that the farmer and the consumer are the two central pillars of India’s sugar policy. The Government has consistently worked to balance the interests of sugarcane farmers with the need to maintain stable and reasonable sugar prices for consumers. From October 1, 2026, with the commencement of the new sugar season, sugarcane farmers will receive the increased Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of ₹365 per quintal. The Government has been increasing FRP every year to ensure remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers while maintaining balance in the sugar sector.
The Government will continue to closely monitor the availability and prices of sugar in the domestic market and take appropriate measures, as necessary, to ensure adequate availability of sugar to consumers as well as the requirements of the food processing and other industries.

The three-day festival, themed “Kadha Rasa Sangama – Confluence of Essence of Stories”, brings together three prominent Kathakali institutions—Sadanam Academy, Kerala Kalamandalam and Margi Theatre—to present three distinctive productions from 18 to 20 September 2026.
Shri K. K. Mishra, IRTS, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, was the Chief Guest at the inaugural ceremony held at 5:45 PM today. Shri Suresh Kumar Chikkala, Director, Kalakshetra Foundation, was also present on the occasion
The festival opened with “Mandodari”, presented by Sadanam Academy. Based on the Ramayana, the production explores the final moments of Ravana’s life and Mandodari’s response to his death.
On 19th  September, Kerala Kalamandalam will present “The Old Man and the Sea”, a Kathakali adaptation of Ernest Hemingway’s celebrated novel. The production portrays the perseverance, determination and struggle of Santiago, the fisherman at the centre of the story.
The festival will conclude on 20th September with “Rugmangada Charitham”, presented by Margi Theatre. The production depicts the devotion of King Rugmangada and the test of his faith and observance of Ekadasi.
As part of the festival, lecture-demonstrations will be conducted from 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM on all three days at Rukmini Arangam, followed by Kathakali presentations by students of the Kalakshetra Foundation.
Established in 1936 by Rukmini Devi Arundale, the Kalakshetra Foundation has played a significant role in the preservation, practice and dissemination of India’s classical arts and traditional cultural heritage. The Foundation has contributed to the development and presentation of Bharatanatyam and has supported the transmission of traditional music, dance and craft traditions through education and performance.

In his address, Shri Shekhawat mentioned the recently held BRICS Summit and said that India's role at the global level and the growing trust of the world in India reflects the country's decisive leadership and its commitment to national interest. He said that even in difficult situations and challenges, India has established its effective role before the world community by keeping national interest’s paramount.
Artists and students of Sangeet Natak Akademi, Kathak Kendra, National School of Drama, Lalit Kala Akademi and Zonal Cultural Centres gave presentations based on Indian classical and cultural traditions at the event.  After the programme, the Union Minister interacted with artists, students, representatives of the National Culture Fund, Adopt a Heritage initiative and other stakeholders and appreciated their contribution in the preservation and promotion of Indian cultural heritage.

content:
The Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) Programme 2026, organised by Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and conducted by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS), concluded today at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The five-day programme, held from September 14 to 18, 2026, brought together senior officers from the three Services and officials from the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs for deliberations on contemporary and emerging national security challenges.
The programme provided a platform for senior military and civil officials to exchange perspectives on jointness, integration, ongoing conflicts, modern ways of warfighting, non-kinetic aspects of national security, defence production and capability development. Discussions also focused on the application of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Quantum Computing, along with cognitive warfare, strategic communication and counter-disinformation operations.
A significant feature of the programme was the participation and direct interaction of senior military leadership with the course participants. The Chief of Defence Staff, Chief of Naval Staff and CISC interacted with the participants and discussed contemporary issues relating to modern-day warfighting, decision-making at the apex level and prevailing security challenges. The Vice Chief of Air Staff and Vice Chief of Army Staff also interacted with the officers and shared their perspectives on contemporary issues.
The programme also witnessed participation from Subject Matter Experts, academia, think tanks and representatives of various Government institutions. The diverse participation facilitated comprehensive discussions on the changing character of warfare and the need for coordinated national responses to emerging security challenges.
The CORE Programme further contributed to strengthening inter-departmental coordination and inter-agency jointness by bringing the Defence Forces, civil ministries and key institutions together on a common platform. The deliberations underscored the importance of closer coordination across diplomatic, informational, economic and military domains and reinforced the need for a Whole-of-Nation approach to national security. Scenario-based exercises on cognitive warfare and strategic communication further enriched the learning and deliberations.

title: HAL hands over 2 LCA FOC Twin Seater Trainers & 3 HTT 40 Basic Trainers to IAF and 4 Dhruv NG helicopters to PHL in the presence of Raksha Mantri & Civil Aviation Minister
subtitle:
The ceremony is a significant milestone in India’s progress towards indigenous aerospace capability, technological self-confidence & Aatmanirbharta: Shri Rajnath Singh

“Indigenous aerospace capability vital for achieving self-reliance & global competitiveness”

RM calls for enhanced public-private synergy to build next-gen indigenous aerospace capabilities

“Young scientists, engineers must develop transformative technologies to secure India’s leadership in global aerospace”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) handed over two Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Final Operational Clearance (FOC) Twin Seater Trainers & three HTT 40 Basic Trainers to the Indian Air Force (IAF), and four Dhruv Next Generation (NG) helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited (PHL) in the presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Minister of Civil Aviation Shri K Rammohan Naidu in Bengaluru, Karnataka on September 18, 2026. In his address, Raksha Mantri described the handing over as a significant milestone in the nation’s progress towards indigenous aerospace capability, technological self-confidence and self-reliance. “Our aim is to make India capable, self-reliant, and globally competitive in meeting its aerospace requirements,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that India is moving systematically towards Aatmanirbharta in defence, as the nation is manufacturing the state-of-the-art equipment indigenously ever since Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government began working with the core mantra of self-reliance. “We’ve taken steps to not only provide the opportunity to Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) to advance in the defence sector, but also encourage the private industry, ensuring a level playing field,” he added, while listing the steps taken by the Ministry of Defence to promote self-reliance.
Raksha Mantri stressed the need to advance systematically in the aerospace sector, terming self-reliance in the domain as the need of the hour. “There can be no sudden ‘big bang’ in the development of aerospace systems. It is a vast and gradual process involving a wide range of components. All the products and components involved represent small rungs on a long ladder; we must move forward one step at a time. Naturally, there would be challenges, but we need to view them as milestones on a larger roadmap to achieve progress in a sector as complex and crucial as aerospace,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh also termed the handing over ceremony as a symbol of the growing synergy between civil aviation and defence aerospace capabilities, emphasising that the development of a robust aerospace industry should not be limited merely to meeting defence requirements. He called for building an ecosystem capable of effectively addressing the needs of both the civil and military aviation sectors. “When capabilities such as aircraft design, avionics, propulsion, composite materials, flight control systems, manufacturing, and certification are developed within the country, they benefit the entire aerospace sector. We must build an integrated aerospace ecosystem which is self-reliant across every domain. I am confident of achieving this endeavour through our collective strength,” he said.
Asserting that the nature of warfare is rapidly evolving, and future air operations will be information-intensive and technology-driven, Raksha Mantri underscored the importance of developing complex systems indigenously. He stated that combat effectiveness can only be ensured through a combination of well-trained personnel, advanced technology, integrated systems, and rapid decision-making, expressing confidence that LCA FOC Trainer will play a crucial role in preparing the pilots for this demanding operational environment. “While the Dhruv-NG exemplifies our indigenous civil aerospace prowess, LCA FOC Trainer stands as a symbol of indigenous military aerospace capability and the maturity of its fighter aircraft ecosystem,” he added.
On the HTT-40, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that India had, for years, relied on imported aircraft to meet its basic training requirements, but HAL is now indigenously manufacturing HTT-40 to cater to the needs of IAF. Highlighting the aircraft’s export potential, he expressed confidence that the HTT-40 would find demand in international markets and fulfil its intended role in strengthening India’s aerospace capabilities.
Raksha Mantri highlighted HAL’s expertise across aircraft manufacturing, helicopter development, overhaul, repair, maintenance and aerospace engineering,  calling it a pillar in India’s endeavour to build indigenous aerospace capabilities. He exhorted the DPSU to further expand its capabilities across the entire aerospace value chain, including design, development, manufacturing, certification, lifecycle support and global marketing.
Shri Rajnath Singh called for realistic project timelines to address delays in ongoing technical projects. He noted that delays can create gaps in meeting critical defence requirements, lead to cost escalations and increase the risk of technology obsolescence.
Terming R&D as a crucial priority area, Raksha Mantri urged young scientists, engineers, designers, test pilots, and technicians to take it as a challenge to create technologies that do not exist today. He called upon them to develop capabilities that secure a leading position for India in the global aerospace technology landscape over the coming decade.
Shri Rajnath Singh stressed the need to not view public and private sectors as competitors, but collaborators. “There is a need for enhanced public-private synergy to build next-gen indigenous aerospace capabilities. By working together, we can accelerate the growth of India’s aerospace sector. We must prepare for the sector’s transformation through Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned aerial systems, electronic warfare, cyber technologies, and next-generation propulsion, with a strong focus on their indigenous development and integration. Let us all resolve to make India not only self-reliant in the field of aerospace technology but also a global leader,” he said.
Speaking on the occasion, Minister of Civil Aviation Shri K Rammohan Naidu said that the certification and induction of the Dhruv NG into civil operations marked an important milestone for India's indigenous civil aviation ecosystem. He termed it as a reflection of the growing capability of Indian industry to develop and support advanced aerospace platforms for commercial applications.
CMD, HAL Shri Ravi K stated that the handover of Tejas FOC Twin Seater Trainers, HTT 40 Basic Trainers and Dhruv NG helicopters demonstrates HAL’s ability to develop and deliver platforms for diverse civil and defence requirements. These two platforms, he added, reflect the depth of capability that HAL has built over the years and the strength of the indigenous aerospace ecosystem that supports them.
Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh; Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar; and Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation Shri Samir Kumar Sinha attended the event.
The LCA Twin Seater Trainers are the final two aircraft under the FOC contract. The aircraft will support the Indian Air Force's training requirements and provide pilots with an indigenous training continuum into frontline fighter operations. The Tejas Trainer retains the core systems and combat capability of the frontline platform, enabling pilots to train on the aircraft they will eventually fly in service.
The HTT-40 (Hindustan Turbo Trainer-40) is an indigenously designed and developed Basic Trainer Aircraft intended to meet the primary training requirements of the Defence Forces. The aircraft is built around a proven turboprop engine and is designed to provide good low-speed handling characteristics and effective training for trainee pilots. It incorporates a modern cockpit and avionics suite and is capable of performing a range of basic training and flying roles, including aerobatics, general handling, instrument flying, navigation, night flying and close formation flying.
The Dhruv NG marks an important step in HAL’s entry into the civil and commercial rotary-wing segment. Configured for civil operations, the helicopter incorporates enhanced systems, modern avionics and a more powerful engine. It is intended for a range of applications including passenger transport, emergency medical services and offshore logistics support.

Raksha Mantri highlighted that before 2014, India faced significant challenges such as corruption and misgovernance which had weakened the morale of the people, and the nation’s progress in the last 12 years has been shaped by its ability to face adversity with confidence and convert challenges into opportunities. “Over the last 12 years, the world has faced a pandemic such as COVID-19 and witnessed several wars, which have had a profound impact on the global economy. Despite global challenges, we are moving steadily on the path towards becoming a self-reliant and developed nation,” he said.

He added that defence exports have risen from nearly Rs 600 crore to around Rs 40,000 crore, with Indian equipment reaching around 100 countries.
Voicing the nation’s resolve to work tirelessly towards its goals with courage and determination, Shri Rajnath Singh described youth as the country’s greatest strength. “Our youth are building start-ups, creating unicorns, developing drones, building hydrogen trains, and making rockets and satellites. Raksha Mantri added that guided by the virtue of compassion, the Government is working to improve the lives of the people, pointing out that over the past 10 to 12 years, more than 250 million people have been lifted out of poverty. He spoke about UPI, which is the world’s largest real-time payment system, and has been adopted by more than 11 countries. He mentioned the schemes such as PM SHRI, Ayushman Bharat, Lakhpati Didi, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, and Ujjwala Yojana, which have made development more inclusive.
Shri Rajnath Singh noted that India has become a source of hope for the world as it has achieved several targets set to fight climate change ahead of schedule, and provided free vaccines to the people in the country & sent more than 300 million vaccines to 100 countries during COVID-19. India is now providing leadership to the world through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance, he added.
Raksha Mantri underlined that India’s development journey is not limited to economic growth, but also involves strengthening national confidence and moving beyond the colonial mindset. Under PM Modi’s leadership, India is witnessing a cultural and civilisational renaissance, he said. Highlighting the importance of civilisational and cultural heritage, he stated that the country’s modernisation should go hand-in-hand with an appreciation of its cultural traditions. “’Sarva Dharma Samabhava’ or equal respect for all faiths has always been at the heart of our civilisational ethos. And yet, because of Western secularism, our Dharma was made to appear as communalism, tradition as backwardness, belief as fanaticism, and faith as superstition,” he added.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the importance of making the younger generation more aware of India’s history, culture and heritage. Greater awareness among youth, he said, would contribute to stronger national consciousness and help build confidence in India’s place in the world. He called upon the youth to contribute to India’s economic, social and technological transformation, saying that a confident, capable and socially inclusive India can emerge as a developed nation and play a greater role in shaping the future of the world.
On the crucial role of media in today’s times, Raksha Mantri stated that journalism is rightly called the fourth pillar of democracy, terming an independent & impartial press as one of the strongest instruments for ensuring accountability. “The role of the media is not merely to report the news. It is also to ask difficult questions, bring the truth before the people, and hold those in power accountable,” he said.

title: Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar Has Evolved into a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Society Movement for Clean Coasts and Safe Seas: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Leads Coastal Clean-Up Drive at Juhu Beach on Eve of International Coastal Cleanup Day, highlights India's unexplored ocean wealth and refers to Deep Ocean Mission launched by PM Sh Narendra Modi as the torchbearer of India's Blue Economy

India’s Coastal Clean-Up Campaign Unites Government, Citizens and Public Figures for Cleaner Seas: Dr. Jitendra Singh

From 75-Day Campaign to Nationwide Movement: Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar Expands Public Participation in Ocean Conservation: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Campaign Mobilises Coastal States and Union Territories, Central Agencies, Students, Volunteers, NGOs, Celebrities and Sporting Personalities Across the Country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Leading the coastal clean-up drive at Juhu Beach on the eve of "International Coastal Cleanup Day" being observed across the world tomorrow, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted India's unexplored ocean wealth and referred to Deep Ocean Mission launched by PM Sh Narendra Modi as the torchbearer of India's Blue Economy.
The Minister said that the ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’ campaign, launched in 2022 during the celebrations of India’s 75th year of Independence, has evolved into a whole-of-government and whole-of-society movement for cleaner coasts and safer seas.
What began as a 75-day inter-ministerial campaign has grown into an annual nationwide initiative around International Coastal Cleanup Day, observed on the third Saturday of September, bringing together government institutions and citizens in a collective effort to protect India’s coastal and marine environment. The 2026 campaign is being conducted from September 12 to 19.
Dr. Jitendra Singh led the coastal clean-up programme at Juhu Beach, Mumbai, organised on the eve of International Coastal Cleanup Day. Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, and BCCI President Mithun Manhas were among those present, along with Directors and senior officials of the Ministry of Earth Sciences and its institutions, public representatives, celebrities, volunteers and other participants. The programme included a mass Ocean Pledge, followed by a hands-on clean-up activity in which Dr. Jitendra Singh joined officials and volunteers in removing plastic and other waste from the shoreline.
The campaign has brought together coastal States and Union Territories, State Governments, Central Government departments and agencies, the Indian Coast Guard, Indian Navy, students, NGOs, volunteers and local communities. Celebrities, public representatives and sporting personalities have also joined the initiative, giving the campaign a wider social reach. The participation of BCCI President Mithun Manhas at Juhu Beach this year further reflected the effort to bring diverse sections of society together for ocean conservation.
The initiative is rooted in India’s growing engagement with its vast maritime domain. Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement of the Deep Ocean Mission from the Red Fort, India has been strengthening its scientific and technological capabilities to explore the deep ocean and understand its resources and ecosystems. The oceans hold significant potential in terms of metals and minerals, fisheries, marine biodiversity and bioresources, making scientific exploration, responsible use and conservation of marine resources important for India’s long-term development.
The Minister said that the benefits of India’s maritime resources can be realised only alongside protection of the health of marine ecosystems. Cleaner beaches, reduced plastic pollution and greater public awareness are therefore essential to maintaining healthy oceans and ensuring sustainable use of marine resources. The campaign seeks to turn this awareness into sustained citizen participation and collective action.
India’s coastline of about 11,098 km extends across its coastal States and Union Territories and supports diverse ecosystems, communities and economic activities. Its scale calls for coordinated action by governments, scientific institutions, coastal communities and citizens to address marine litter and protect fragile coastal ecosystems.
The 2026 edition of ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’, being conducted from September 12 to 19, features coastal clean-up drives and a range of public-engagement activities across the country. The campaign is bringing together citizens, students, coastal communities, educational institutions, NGOs, volunteer organisations and government agencies as part of a nationwide effort to promote ocean conservation and responsible environmental practices. The Ministry of Earth Sciences and its institutions are supporting the campaign through scientific and public-outreach initiatives related to marine litter and coastal environmental protection.
Citizen participation is also being strengthened through the Sagar Prahari platform, which enables public engagement with the campaign and supports documentation of marine litter. The initiative complements the larger objective of combining scientific understanding with public participation in addressing marine pollution and protecting coastal ecosystems.
The Juhu Beach programme brought together government representatives, sporting personalities, public figures, volunteers and citizens in a common effort to protect India’s coastline. The mass pledge and clean-up activity reinforced the message that keeping India’s shores clean and its seas safe is a shared responsibility, requiring sustained participation well beyond a single day or campaign.
The ‘Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar’ campaign continues to build on the spirit of collective action with which it was launched during India’s 75th year of Independence, strengthening public participation for cleaner beaches, healthier oceans and a more sustainable maritime future.
