n total, SHS 2025 saw the participation of 18.06 crore people across the country. SHS 2025, thus, extended Swachhata from cleanliness activities into community celebration and sustainable practices.
Beyond Cleanliness: Shaping Everyday Behaviour
The SHS journey shows a gradual expansion in the meaning of cleanliness. The early editions focused on cleanliness action and volunteerism. Later editions brought plastic waste, visual cleanliness, and garbage management into focus
. The shift became clearer from
2023 onwards
. “Garbage-Free India” expanded attention towards public spaces and waste management. The 2024 theme then connected cleanliness with
Swabhav and Sanskaar
. In 2025,
Swachhotsav
brought cleanliness into festivals and community celebrations.
In 2026,
Swachhata Mein Sahbhag
places
collective action and cooperation
at the centre.
The campaign has evolved from cleaning physical spaces to fostering
sustained behavioural change
, embedding Swachhata in everyday practices and strengthening a sense of
shared community responsibility
.

title: NHRC, India’s fifth ITEC Executive capacity-building programme on human rights for NHRIs of the Global South concludes in New Delhi
subtitle:
The Commission organised the programme in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

In his valedictory address, NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian calls for stronger cooperation among Global South NHRIs

Says, sharing experiences, addressing challenges and learning from mistakes contribute to institutional learning and improvement

Several eminent speakers addressed the 38 senior functionaries from 14 NHRIs of the Global South on various aspects of governance and human rights
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The six-day Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Executive Capacity Building Programme on human rights for National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs) of the Global South successfully concluded in New Delhi. The programme was organised by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). The valedictory session was addressed by NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian, in the presence of Joint Secretaries, Shri Samir Kumar and Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchhuak and other senior officers.
The programme, which began on 14th September 2026, witnessed participation of 38 senior functionaries from 14 NHRIs of Algeria, Chile, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan, Malaysia, Oman, Samoa, South Africa, Tajikistan and Zimbabwe. It included interactive sessions with eminent persons and domain experts in which participants were introduced to various aspects of civil and political rights as well as socio-economic and cultural rights.
The speakers included NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian, Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal, Director General (Investigation), Smt. Anupama Nilekar Chandra, UN Resident Coordinator, India, Mr. Stefan Priesner, NHRC, India Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar, Former Secretary, Govt. of India, Smt. Bhamathi Balasubramaniam, Prof. (Dr.) Vartika Nanda, Indian Prison Reformer & Founder, Tinka Tinka Foundation, Prof. (Dr.) Pratap Sharan, Head of Psychiatry Department, AIIMS, Dr.Purva Mittal, NHRC, India Special Monitor and Shri Chandra Mishra, Founder, Beggar Corporation. The programme was also enriched by the experiences shared by functionaries of various NHRIs.
In his closing remarks, NHRC, India Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian, expressed his heartfelt gratitude to all the participants for their camaraderie and positive energy during the programme. He said the Capacity-Building Programme goes beyond explaining international human rights instruments, as their practical application varies according to the historical, cultural, social and economic contexts of different countries. Drawing an analogy from science, he said that NHRIs work in the “laboratory” of human rights, where sharing experiences, addressing challenges and learning from mistakes contribute to institutional learning and improvement.
Justice Ramasubramanian expressed appreciation for the active participation of the delegates and emphasised the importance of friendship, cooperation and mutual understanding among NHRIs in advancing human dignity, peace and mutual respect. He also acknowledged the need for stronger cooperation among NHRIs of the Global South and formalising a common platform for collaboration.
The participants lauded NHRC, India and MEA for organising this programme. They appreciated the opportunity to learn about various aspects of human rights, good governance and the Indian ethos of respecting human rights in a democracy with diverse social, cultural, religious and linguistic identities. The participants also got the opportunity to visit iconic places like Rashtrapati Bhawan, Red Fort and TajMahal to have an immersive experience of India’s rich cultural heritage.
NHRC, India Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar presented an overview of the training programme, noting that participants from 46 countries and nearly 200 representatives from various NHRIs have been part of this initiative. He emphasised the need for a nuanced approach while upholding the universality of human rights and appreciated the participants’ active engagement and valuable exchange of knowledge and experiences throughout the programme.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a four-year-old girl after falling into an uncovered manhole near her house in Palwal, Haryana
subtitle: Issues notices to the Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police, Palwal for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 SEP 2026 11:43AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that a four-year-old girl died after falling into an uncovered manhole while playing near her house in Palwal, Haryana on 14th September 2026. Reportedly, despite several complaints by the local residents to the concerned authorities, the manhole remained uncovered.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Deputy Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police, Palwal, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the next of kin of the deceased.
According to the media report, carried out on 16th September 2026, the victim girls' family and local residents found her inside the uncovered manhole and took her in critical condition to the District Civil Hospital, where the doctors declared her dead.

content:
The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, along with the
National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA),
seven National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education
and
Research (NIPERs)
,
Pharmaceutical & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)
and
Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)
–
Bengal Chemical & Pharmaceutical Ltd. (BCPL), Hindustan Antibiotics Limited (HAL), and Karnataka Antibiotics And Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (KAPL)
– will actively participate in
Special Campaign 6.0
from
2nd October to 31st October 2026
. The initiative aims to institutionalize
Swachhata culture
and streamline government functioning by eliminating office pendency.
The campaign is structured in two operational phases:
Preparatory Phase
(15th – 30th September 2026)
:
Identification of target sites, pendency auditing and e-waste mapping.
Implementation Phase
(2nd – 31st October 2026)
:
Execution of cleanliness drives, scrap disposal, and grievance redressal.
Focus Areas for Special Campaign 6.0 :
E-Waste Management :
Safe collection, segregation, and disposal of electronic scrap in accordance with E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.
Grievance & Reference Resolution :
Accelerated disposal of pending MP References, State Government Communications, PMO References, Parliamentary Assurances, Public Grievances, and CPGRAMS Appeals.
Field Office Outreach :
Active participation from field offices, PSUs and NIPERs to conduct outdoor cleanliness drives, office beautification, and sustainability drives.
Through these measures, the Department of Pharmaceuticals reaffirms its commitment to transparent governance, efficient public service delivery and sustainable office management.
